data.title: GrubMarket launches AI Agent to turn invoices into purchase orders
data.description:
GrubMarket, a South San Francisco, California-based software-as-a-service (SAAS) company working with food producers, wholesalers, distributors and retailers, is expanding its use of artificial intelligence (AI) with a new AI agent. The company designed its new AI agent to turn vendor invoices and receipts into purchase orders for food distributors. The tool, called the “AI Orders – Purchase Order Agent,” was made to reduce the amount of manual data entry required from produce and other fresh food distributors.

“The food supply chain industry is undergoing unprecedented transformation driven by artificial intelligence,” said Mike Xu, CEO of GrubMarket, in a release statement. “With our new AI Orders – Purchase Order Agent, we are bringing powerful AI capabilities to another critical function within food distribution.”

The new agent follows other recent AI rollouts from GrubMarket. In June, the company announced the launch of an AI sales agent. Its other AI deployments have included a reporting AI agent on its GrubAssist AI platform. GrubMarket also created its Monitoring AI Agent that tracks financial and operational data for customers.

Now, the technology provider is turning to purchase orders.

Why GrubMarket launched its new AI agent

Xu said that by automating purchasing workflows, GrubMarket is helping distributors operate more efficiently. In turn, he believes that they can gain better visibility into their businesses, making better-informed decisions and improving profitability.

“This launch represents another important step in our broader vision of building specialized AI agents that automate and optimize every major function across the food supply chain industry,” Xu said, adding that the company remains committed to leveraging artificial intelligence to help businesses modernize their operations and unlock new levels of efficiency and growth.

Industry observers said the real test will be in the details.

Amy Dean, vice president of operations at SC Codeworks, a Columbus, Ohio-based warehouse management software company, said that every company handles purchase order entry differently. However, she sees it is most likely being driven by spreadsheets, ERP systems and planners.

“AI has the potential to reduce repetitive data entry, which would free up employees to handle exceptions, vendor relationships, and more strategic purchasing activities,” Dean said.

She noted AI will need to navigate special challenges that come with the food business.

“Food distribution especially is not always straightforward,” she assessed. “There are many variables that change often, such as recalls, substitutions, and vendor-specific requirements.”

Dean, who is an operations and IT expert with over a decade of experience in logistics, believes that it will be “critical that all of that is accounted for in the logic that is used with an AI agent.”

Moreover, she sees access to accurate data as a vital part of the new agent’s success.

“The ability for an AI agent to read invoices, receipts and photos could be beneficial for organizations that don’t currently utilize integration tools,” Dean stated. “However, that AI agent is only as effective as the data it has access to. This is where inventory accuracy becomes critical and current business processes can make or break the success.”

Larger challenges for the new agent

Dmytro Klymentiev is an AI systems engineer in Chicago who builds AI automation and ERP systems for businesses. He said reading a photo of an invoice and pulling out the line items is no longer the hard part. In his view, that is because most current AI models can do it. What GrubMarket adds, he said, is the connection. The extracted data becomes a structured purchase order inside the distributor’s own system, matched to its catalog.

“That is useful, but I would call it an incremental step rather than a new way of purchasing,” Klymentiev said.

In his view, the time savings are narrower than they look. He pointed out that while nobody needs to type out an order, someone may still need to check each draft to avoid knock-on effects from errors.

“A misread quantity or a wrong product match turns into a wrong order, then a wrong delivery, a failed invoice match and wrong stock levels,” Klymentiev stated. “The work moves from data entry to review, and the review has to be careful.”

Before adopting a tool like this, he recommends that distributors ask whether it flags a line or guesses when it’s unsure, how it matches products to their catalog, what happens with new or renamed items, and whether they can measure its error rate on their own documents before it touches live orders.

data.title: Lowe's partners with Bilt to expand loyalty rewards, AI-powered commerce
data.description:
Lowe’s Companies Inc. has partnered with housing rewards platform Bilt to expand its loyalty reach. The partnership lets Bilt members earn points on Lowe’s purchases and use those rewards toward a home maintenance subscription.

Announced Nov. 10, the tie-up makes Lowe’s Bilt’s exclusive home improvement partner, connecting the retailer with the platform’s more than 8 million members. The companies also plan to launch a curated Lowe’s marketplace within Bilt in early 2027.

“By partnering with Bilt, we can meet customers in a community they already know and love and connect them to Lowe’s products, services and rewards in a way that feels simple and seamless,” said Jen Wilson, Lowe’s executive vice president and chief marketing officer, in the company’s announcement.

The partnership runs on Bilt’s new Neighborhood OS. The artificial intelligence (AI)-powered commerce platform helps businesses reach nearby consumers with personalized offers and loyalty benefits.

Lowe’s ranks No. 9 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Lowe’s is No. 90 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

How Lowe’s and Bilt rewards work together

Bilt members can now earn rewards through both loyalty programs.

Its members can link an existing MyLowe’s Rewards account — or create one — to earn one Bilt Point per dollar on eligible Lowe’s purchases. Additionally, they can earn MyLowe’s Money through the retailer’s loyalty program. MyLowe’s Rewards benefits include free shipping and exclusive member deals.

The agreement adds Lowe’s to Bilt’s network of more than 50,000 merchant partners nationwide, including restaurants and fitness studios. Through Neighborhood OS, Lowe’s can reach members with offers and rewards based on where they live and direct them to nearby stores.

The partnership also gives members another way to pay for Lowe’s home maintenance services. Bilt members can use Bilt Points, Bilt Cash or a linked payment card to purchase a Lowe’s HomeCare+ subscription, the companies said.

The subscription costs $99 annually and includes two in-home visits by trained Lowe’s associates, covering up to seven maintenance services. Subscribers also receive 5% off products used during those services and Gold MyLowe’s Rewards benefits. HomeCare+ is available in select ZIP codes and renews each year automatically.

Bilt’s Neighborhood OS manages enrollment, checks service availability at members’ addresses and processes subscription payments, Lowe’s said. The companies plan to add matching with existing MyLowe’s Rewards accounts in December.

How Bilt Neighborhood OS uses AI to connect businesses and shoppers

Bilt’s Neighborhood OS connects with businesses’ existing payment, reservation and customer-management systems. This allows merchants to target nearby shoppers with offers, recognize returning customers and track spending tied to promotions.

“For example, a neighborhood restaurant can identify prospective customers, launch a targeted offer to bring them in, recognize them when they visit, and automatically apply the appropriate benefit through its existing point-of-sale system,” Bilt said in its announcement.

The platform also uses AI agents to manage tasks such as reservations, customer communications and marketing across those connected systems.

In the 30 days before its announcement, Bilt said its AI agents completed more than 2 million actions across more than 29,000 businesses, with 91% of those actions requiring no human intervention.

The platform builds on Bilt’s expansion beyond rent rewards. Founded in 2021, the company has added mortgage rewards, local shopping, travel and home services.

Bilt estimates that roughly $6.6 trillion in annual U.S. retail and food-services spending takes place in person. Its members generated more than $12 billion in rewarded commerce at local businesses over the past 12 months, the company said.

How loyalty rewards influence shopping behavior

Lowe’s brings an established loyalty program to the partnership. MyLowe’s Rewards had more than 30 million members, who shopped twice as often and spent more than 50% more than nonmembers, the retailer said in its 2025 annual report.

Bilt’s research points to consumers’ willingness to try nearby businesses that offer rewards. In its first-ever State of the Neighborhood 2026 study, 95% of respondents said they would try a local business at least once if they could earn points or rewards there. Another 87% said they would shop more frequently at a local business offering those incentives.

The study also found that two-thirds of Americans make at least 80% of their everyday spending within their neighborhoods, with the median consumer shopping within 15 miles of home. Conducted by 451 Research by S&P Global on Bilt’s behalf, the survey covered 6,591 U.S. adults in March and April 2026.

Bilt expands partnerships across retail, technology and services

data.title: e.l.f. Beauty Q2 sales grow 51% as it embraces digital platforms
data.description:
E.l.f. Beauty Inc. raised its full-year outlook for the second straight quarter after net sales increased 51% in its fiscal Q2 2027, helped by Rhode’s launch at Sephora in Europe and a rebound in unit sales for the core e.l.f. brand.

Net sales for the quarter ended Sept. 30 reached $520.8 million, an increase from $343.9 million a year earlier. It was the company’s 31st consecutive quarter of net sales growth, CEO Tarang Amin said. 

E.l.f. said sales grew in both retailer and ecommerce channels in the U.S. and abroad.

Organic net sales rose about 35%, chief financial officer Mandy Fields said on the earnings call. Rhode, which e.l.f. acquired in August 2025, added about 16 percentage points to total growth in the month before the deal’s anniversary on Aug. 5.

E.l.f. Beauty ranks No. 328 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database, which ranks North America’s leading online retailers by annual web sales.

E.l.f. Beauty is also No. 327 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

Amazon and TikTok Shop drive digital sales

Connected commerce, which e.l.f. uses to describe sales through online platforms, accounted for 31% of sales in Q2, Amin said. 

In the U.S., e.l.f. was the top cosmetics brand on Amazon and the most-searched. On TikTok Shop, e.l.f. Cosmetics climbed to No. 2 in cosmetics.

Amazon ranks No. 3 in Digital Commerce 360’s Global Online Marketplaces Database. That database ranks the 100 largest such marketplaces by third-party gross merchandise value (GMV).

E.l.f. is also using digital platforms to test new categories. In October, the retailer launched e.l.f. Pop, a fragrance and body collection, exclusively on Amazon and TikTok Shop, with more scents planned later this fiscal year. E.l.f. Hair launched in July with a six-product assortment priced at $10 or less, exclusively at Target. It is already among Target’s top 20 hair care brands, Amin said, and about half its buyers are new to e.l.f.

Rhode’s direct-to-consumer site remains a strong channel alongside its retail expansion, Amin said. A limited-edition collection with influencer Alexandra Leclerc had a waitlist of more than 200,000 people and mostly sold out within an hour. E.l.f. has not seen higher customer acquisition costs for Rhode, he said.

Rhode’s European launch lifts international sales

Rhode launched at Sephora in 19 European countries in September. Amin said the launch marked “the biggest launch in Sephora’s history.” He also said Rhode is the top brand Sephora carries in Europe, with one of the strongest repeat rates the retailer sees. Rhode is still in only about 40% of Sephora locations worldwide, he said.

E.l.f. international net sales grew 165% in Q2, while U.S. net sales rose 25%. International sales accounted for about 25% of net sales on a trailing 12-month basis. In May, Digital Commerce 360 reported the figure was about 20%. Amin said legacy beauty peers generate about 70% of their sales abroad.

Fields said the core e.l.f. brand also improved in its largest international markets: Canada, the U.K. and Germany.

e.l.f. expects growth to slow in second half of 2027

E.l.f. now expects fiscal 2027 net sales growth of 22% to 24%, up from a projected 18% to 20% last quarter and 12% to 14% in May. 

The beauty retailer expects second-half net sales growth of about 7-10%, with Q3 above that range and Q4 below it. Fields tied the Q4 slowdown to last year’s launches, including e.l.f.’s expanded space at Ulta Beauty, its launch with dm in Germany, Rhode’s launch at MECCA in Australia and New Zealand and Naturium’s first expansion into Walmart.

Fields said the 7% to 10% growth outlook is well ahead of the beauty category, which is growing at a low-single-digit rate.

data.title: 3 online sales factors to watch in 2026 holiday shopping forecasts
data.description:
Online retailers preparing for the 2026 holiday shopping season are about to face a wave of customers unlike any they have seen in previous years, as forecasts call for ecommerce sales to grow at a rate similar to 2025.

The Cyber 5, a period which includes Thanksgiving Day, Black Friday and the three days that follow, begins on Nov. 26 in 2026, concluding on Cyber Monday, which falls on Nov. 30. Over those days, artificial intelligence (AI) and agentic commerce will be put to use through new offerings for shoppers from Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and other providers, which are trying to command larger roles in research, payments and more. Meanwhile, online retailers will put their own new tools to the test, as they cater to a rising share of AI-associated traffic referrals and AI agents that are browsing their ecommerce sites on behalf of human users.

As consumers continue to face pressure from inflation, tariff-related costs and other macroeconomic factors, online shoppers care about how AI options such as Google’s Gemini and Meta’s Muse can help them compare prices and find deals. In fact, 26% of online shoppers surveyed in October by Digital Commerce 360 and Bizrate Insights said that this was their primary reason for using AI when buying products.

In the meantime, retailers’ ecommerce sites, ChatGPT apps and optimization strategies for content and catalog data will all play roles in their pursuit of traffic and conversion that helps them to meet their year-end sales targets.

Sales projections for the 2026 holiday shopping season

Adobe’s forecast for the final two months of 2026 calls for online sales to grow 6.7% year over year to reach $275.1 billion. That growth would be comparable to — but slightly down from — the 6.8% growth achieved in 2025 by Adobe’s own measurements.

A wider forecast from Deloitte, published in September, set expectations for total holiday retail sales (including ecommerce and physical stores) at $1.70 trillion to $1.71 trillion for activity in November 2026 through January 2027. Sales at that level would mean growth of 4.0 to 4.8% from a year earlier, after that year-ago period saw 4.1% year-over-year growth.

Meanwhile, November results published by the International Council of Shopping Centers on Nov. 18 showed that 88% of 1,007 U.S. adults surveyed planned to shop at some point during the Cyber 5. The same report showed that 77% expected to spend the same or more than they did in 2025.

“Shoppers are increasingly willing to switch and/or try new brands in order to find the best value — making Thanksgiving Weekend a prime opportunity for retailers to earn their business,” said Tom McGee, president and CEO of the ICSC. “With AI giving consumers more tools than ever to research products, compare prices, and find deals, shoppers are taking a more active role in deciding where their money goes.”

Increasing AI traffic conversion

Adobe projects that AI-associated referral traffic to online retailers’ websites will be up 159% on Thanksgiving, 95% on Black Friday and 88% on Cyber Monday from its previous levels in 2025. Those percentages are significantly smaller than the four-digit percentages of year-over-year growth seen during various periods in 2025. However, another key metric has been moving upward, according to Adobe analysts — and that is the conversion rate for AI-referred shoppers.

In August, Adobe Analytics shared that it has seen AI-referrals’ conversion rates outperform non-AI referrals for 11 consecutive months, with AI referrals generating 53% more revenue per visit than other shoppers. Then, in September, Adobe observed that difference to be 83% higher per visit when compared with non-AI traffic. That was the largest gap observed in 2026 and an inverted relationship from a year earlier. Essentially, Adobe saw AI-associated traffic go from being less effective, worth less than half the value of non-AI-referred visits, to being worth nearly twice as much.

Elsewhere, Salesforce predicted that AI agents would be responsible for 20% of all 2026 holiday ecommerce traffic in 2026, according to Caila Schwartz, director of consumer strategy and insights for Salesforce. Schwartz wrote in July that her company, which provides an ecommerce platform for retailers, expects to see 1 in 3 ecommerce sites using personal, site-specific agents to serve shoppers during the period it calls Cyber Week (the Tuesday before Thanksgiving and six days that follow) in 2026.

Discount levels and windows for online holiday discounts

Deep discounts for the season began as far back as October in 2026, with Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days at the beginning of the month. Online shoppers spent $9.86 billion on Oct. 6 and 7, as that event played out, according to Adobe. Looking ahead, the company’s forecast assesses that discounts during the Cyber 5 (which Adobe refers to as Cyber Week) would reach up to 30% off listed prices.

Adobe anticipates that those discounts will hit 21% in the days immediately preceding Thanksgiving and then settle into 10% to 15% during December. Ultimately, those deals would be roughly in line with the levels seen for the 2025 holiday season.

“Sales and discounts (56%) are the most cited factors in shoppers’ decision-making around which retailers to shop throughout the holiday season,” wrote Lea Grgich, a senior research analyst at the National Retail Federation.

The industry group released its own survey results on October 28, showing that 64% of shoppers expected to wait until Thanksgiving to do most of their holiday shopping in 2026. That was up from 51% in 2020.

data.title: Tractor Supply joins Uber Marketplace, adding delivery options for rural customers
data.description:
Tractor Supply Co. is adding Uber as a delivery partner, making its products available through the Uber, Uber Eats and Postmates apps. The companies announced the nationwide partnership Nov. 12.

Customers can order pet food, animal care products, lawn and garden supplies, tools and outdoor gear for on-demand delivery. Tractor Supply operated 2,486 stores in 49 states as of Sept. 26, along with 135 Petsense by Tractor Supply stores. The announcement refers to Tractor Supply’s stores, not Petsense locations.

Tractor Supply is No. 83 in the Top 1000 Database. The database tracks North America’s largest online retailers, ranking them by annual ecommerce sales and more.

Tractor Supply expands delivery beyond metro areas

Uber’s pitch centers on geography. Tractor Supply stores are concentrated in rural, exurban and suburban communities, which Uber sees as an opportunity to extend on-demand delivery beyond major cities.

“The need for convenience doesn’t stop at the city limits,” said Nathan Bernheim, Uber’s head of retail partnerships, in the announcement.

Matthew Rubin, Tractor Supply’s senior vice president and president of digital and ecommerce, said the deal gives customers more ways to shop. It also introduces the retailer to “millions of Uber users” who may not have shopped there before, he said. “Tractor Supply is continually finding new ways to serve customers and make Life Out Here more convenient,” Rubin added.

Customers can search for Tractor Supply in the Uber, Uber Eats or Postmates app, or browse the Retail section. They then pick a store, build a cart, choose a delivery option and track the order in the app. 

To mark the launch, Uber is offering $20 off Tractor Supply orders of $60 or more. Fees and terms apply.

The announcement did not specify delivery speeds or fees.

Tractor Supply’s relationship with Instacart and DoorDash

Uber is the second delivery platform Tractor Supply added this year. In July, the retailer announced it had joined Instacart Marketplace, a competitor to Uber. 

At the time of the announcement, Tractor Supply and Instacart representatives shared similar sentiments about expanding same-day delivery to rural customers and introducing Tractor Supply to new shoppers.

Tractor Supply has also had a delivery partnership with DoorDash since 2022. Now the delivery market is consolidating. 

On Oct. 29, DoorDash announced that it would acquire Instacart in a deal valued at $17 billion. The deal needs regulatory and Instacart shareholder approval. The companies expect it to close near the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028.

Until then, Instacart will operate independently. DoorDash expects to keep the Instacart brand, app and enterprise technology products afterward.

Tractor Supply’s own delivery network

The Uber deal builds on a store-based delivery network Tractor Supply has spent the past year and a half expanding. CEO Hal Lawton said in September that the retailer has offered delivery from stores for five or six years, including same-day and two- to three-day options. Its newer “Final Mile” system links every three to four stores in a hub-and-spoke arrangement, with one store serving four.

Tractor Supply completed as many last-mile deliveries in the first half of 2026 as it did in all of 2025, Lawton said. Delivery from stores led double-digit digital sales growth in fiscal Q2, even as comparable store sales fell 1.5% in a difficult quarter.

The retailer is also building out its supply chain. In September, Tractor Supply opened its 11th distribution center in Nampa, Idaho, an 865,000-square-foot facility that will support 123 stores across nine states in its first year. The center was designed to serve more than 200 stores at full capacity.
